driven: driven_net (unnamed in chunk, combinational output of expression)

guarantees.claim: A combinational net is driven with the value: prim_mubi_pkg::mubi4_test_false_loose(prim_mubi_pkg::mubi4_t'(reg2hw.range_regwen.q)) && (reg2hw.enabled_memory_range_base.qe || reg2hw.enabled_memory_range_limit.qe).

uncertain_points.claim: The combinational net driven by this expression is unlabeled in the chunk and its downstream use is unknown. The condition becomes true when range_regwen.q indicates the register write-enable is not in a locked (false) multi-bit state AND either enabled_memory_range_base.qe or enabled_memory_range_limit.qe is asserted. If this net enables a memory range window or other access control, it may incorrectly permit DMA access while range_regwen is unlocked and an error flag is present.
uncertain_points.risk: Security bypass: a locked range_regwen combined with a stale or spurious error (qe) could grant access to a protected memory range.

security_implications: This chunk combines a multi-bit register write-enable test (mubi4_test_false_loose on range_regwen.q) with error flags from memory range base/limit configuration registers. If the resulting signal is used as a memory-range enable condition, a false test outcome (indicating range_regwen is not in the locked state) together with an active error flag could erroneously open a protected range, potentially allowing unauthorized DMA transactions to sensitive memory regions. The exact propagation path must be verified in Phase3 source review.
